selection.ordinary_rule: For each of the nine historical contribution domains, select the minimum SHA-256(seed + claim ID) among descriptive claims excluding risk IDs. Reproduced exactly.
selection.amendment: After aggregate access-class inventory, before reopening IND-S06, add IND-K08 as 20th claim because 17/129 records are partial-text/abstract and the initial risk selection did not explicitly cover one. Ordinary sample unchanged; no adverse source-check result selected this addition.
selection.selection_limitation: Purposive risk and hash-selected descriptive controls; not an error-rate estimator. SYN claims and new-wave dossiers are outside the selected source audit.

verdict_definitions.supported: The specified observation, attributed statement or bounded logical inference is directly supported by the inspected passage. This is not replication.
verdict_definitions.qualified: The statement is faithful as currently bounded, but source access, reconstruction, identification or measurement limits materially constrain what can be concluded. Qualification is not automatically a defect or a request to lower its label.
verdict_definitions.defective: The sampled assertion contradicts, misstates or materially exceeds inspected support.
verdict_definitions.unresolved: Available material does not permit a source-entailment verdict.

assessment: No sampled historical statement was shown false or materially unsupported as bounded. Ten supported and ten qualified verdicts; one nonblocking precision recommendation. This does not accept the whole edition or validate unreviewed claims.

claim_audit.assessment: The scanned observation names IR64 in September 1988 and a subsequent high-yielding variety within the coordinated Manuaba calendar. The later narrative is inherited from Lansing, not a second independent observation.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: Retain the site/date boundary and descriptive-only status.

claim_audit.inspected_locator: AGR-S08 pp.2362–2369, equation 12 and section IV.B; pp.2378–2379
claim_audit.assessment: The 44% fixed-allocation estimate and 90-country baseline are supported. Page 2369 specifies the average country; release-timing assumptions and alternative innovation remain consequential.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: Clarify the averaging unit; no re-estimation was performed.

claim_audit.assessment: The cash/insurance comparisons support increased investment and risk exposure. Table III is the first stage; Table IV instruments insurance receipt using randomized prices and requires an exclusion assumption.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: This is stronger than an observational association, but not a universal constraint ranking or welfare result.

claim_audit.assessment: Operating Roman watermills and reported enslaved hydraulic maintenance defeat the absolute institutional-incompatibility proposition as framed.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: Neither source identifies the legal status of Barbegal workers or a marginal labour-cost effect.

claim_audit.inspected_locator: ANC-S06 §§III and V, especially Urso/Venafrum and private grants
claim_audit.assessment: Bannon explicitly distinguishes personal grants from property rights, combines fees/status with open-access fountains, and documents local administration.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: Rules and selected examples do not establish actual equal access; inscriptions were read through Bannon.

claim_audit.inspected_locator: DIG-S09 pp.1288–1292, equations 1–2 and attrition discussion
claim_audit.assessment: The paper reports the approximately 194,000-household extrapolation using early agent expansion and 2014 outcomes. The record correctly distinguishes estimation from a counted beneficiary total.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: High attrition, rollout selection and extrapolation remain material; supplementary tables and raw data were not replicated.

claim_audit.assessment: The filed table reports $1,896 million revenue and $16,120 million operating loss for Reality Labs in 2023; the segment includes AR, mixed reality and VR.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: Company segment accounting does not identify active users, retention or per-headset economics.

claim_audit.inspected_locator: IND-S04 January 2002 text p.13 and Table 3 p.23
claim_audit.assessment: The version explicitly gives less than 0.01 percentage points before 1830 and a larger railway-era contribution. The inspected table is consistent with that bounded claim.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: This is faithful reporting of a reconstruction, not validation of steam stocks or later scholarship.

claim_audit.assessment: Devine reports slightly under one-quarter in 1909 and over 53% in 1919, while explaining the lack of comprehensive unit-drive configuration data.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: Horsepower capacity must remain distinct from establishment adoption and factory redesign.

claim_audit.assessment: Linked incumbents and later young cohorts have different observed outcomes, as stated. Incumbent occupational income scores are proxies, and linkage is selective.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: Preserve cohort definitions, local comparisons and observation intervals; the results do not measure continuous unemployment duration.

claim_audit.assessment: The authors expressly cannot exclude wage changes of approximately plus or minus 10%; the smaller wage sample has 72 cutovers versus 261 in the main sample.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: This is a power limitation, not proof of zero effect or a shared interval for every subgroup.

claim_audit.assessment: Wagner regards the often-repeated output figure as plausible but rejects the reliability of Hartwell’s quota-based calculation. The record accurately preserves that distinction.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: The review did not independently inspect the Chinese fiscal sources or reconstruct output.

claim_audit.assessment: The experiment supports task-dependent hardness/working-property trade-offs. The paper itself notes difficulty obtaining reproducible elongation measurements.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: A modern alloy comparison does not establish ancient selection motives; alloy concentration and processing matter.

claim_audit.assessment: Boylston reproduces the Timonius, Mather/Onesimus and Pylarinius reports, including women practitioners. The record uses these as transmission evidence and avoids a precise-origin claim.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: The original correspondence was not independently acquired; specific geographical identities in the secondary account are not needed for this claim.

claim_audit.assessment: The preferred estimate is 26.6 of 79.2 log points in the treated setting, with complementarity between the interventions. Boston is excluded from estimation.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: This is a conditional local estimate; composition/pre-trend checks do not establish random rollout or universal effects.

claim_audit.inspected_locator: MOB-S08 January 2015 version §2.1, printed pp.5–6 and Fig.1
claim_audit.assessment: The stated western mining/military route and eastern route sequence, including wartime delays and Kumasi in 1923, match the source.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: This confirms faithful use of the authors’ reconstruction; the colonial records and cited railway histories were not independently reopened.

claim_audit.inspected_locator: MOB-S11 published 2016 article p.37, Tables 2–3 and pp.44–46
claim_audit.assessment: The article distinguishes large adoption-timing estimates from smaller product comparisons and explicitly reports failed pre-trend robustness.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: The stronger product comparison remains design-dependent; no pooled general-equilibrium or port-specific return is established.

claim_audit.inspected_locator: NET-S03 pp.2–3, Reference collection and preceding discussion
claim_audit.assessment: The collection has 228 papers, 133 undated, and 83 dated to the eighteenth/nineteenth centuries; the text explains trade and finishing obstacles to manufacturing attribution.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: Neither text language nor this conservation collection is a medieval adoption denominator.

claim_audit.assessment: Schwartz distinguishes unlocated alleged Bayezid/Selim bans from the 1588 protection of printed-book merchants and traces inherited assertions.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: This verifies the source’s bounded documentary argument, not the nonexistence of every restriction or a new archival search.

claim_audit.assessment: The abstract expressly attributes unbuilt large schemes to coordination and collective funding. The record accurately labels this as Malm’s argument and low-confidence, abstract-only evidence.
claim_audit.remaining_limit: Scheme feasibility and causal weight remain unresolved; the full article was not acquired.

findings.finding: The 44% figure is faithfully reported, but the compact statement and report omit the source’s explicit average-country unit.
findings.evidence: AGR-S08 section IV.B, printed p.2369, following equation 12.
findings.recommended_change: Add “in the average country” and p.2369 to the locator. Keep fixed allocations and identification limits.
findings.acceptance_check: Inspect the changed claim and report plus their compiled ledger; do not substitute a global output-weighted or farmer-level percentage.
findings.does_not_establish: No numerical contradiction or invalidity of the econometric estimate is established.

additional_scholarship.publication: Jonell, Jones, Lucas and Naylor (2024), Limited waterpower contributed to rise of steam power in British Cottonopolis
additional_scholarship.inspected: Introduction, waterpower potential/results, basin comparisons, reservoirs discussion and methods
additional_scholarship.assessment: High-resolution historical waterpower reconstruction finds geographically concentrated scarcity. This gives the existing physical-reliability rival concrete evidence; it does not isolate the fate of Malm’s individual reservoir schemes.
additional_scholarship.next_step: Compare matching basin, period and scheme constraints before elevating the coordination hypothesis; do not treat the model as a replicated adoption treatment effect.

additional_scholarship.status: alternative mechanism; compatible with bounded ban criticism
additional_scholarship.publication: Titus Nemeth (2022), Overlooked: The Role of Craft in the Adoption of Typography in the Muslim Middle East
additional_scholarship.inspected: pp.21–24, craft/reading discussion and conclusion pp.49–52
additional_scholarship.assessment: Accepts the missing blanket-ban evidence while arguing that formal typography and reading conventions deserve causal attention. It does not restore the alleged decrees.
additional_scholarship.next_step: Treat craft/legibility as a testable additional mechanism; do not convert modern reading evidence into a measured historical effect.

additional_scholarship.status: critique adjudicated; no demonstrated numerical rebuttal
additional_scholarship.publication: Bateman, Duvendack and Loubere (2019), Is Fin-Tech the New Panacea for Poverty Alleviation and Local Development?
additional_scholarship.assessment: Raises displacement, external-validity and selection concerns. Its assertion that the original lacks a counterfactual is not supported by the original equations and comparison design. No replication establishes a corrected poverty count here.
additional_scholarship.next_step: Retain unresolved spillover/general-equilibrium questions and inspect original supplementary/replication material before stronger claims.

additional_scholarship.status: external-validity contrast; not a same-sample replication
additional_scholarship.publication: Aidt, Davenport and Gray (2023), New perspectives on the contribution of sanitary investments to mortality decline in English cities, 1845–1909
additional_scholarship.inspected: Accepted manuscript pp.2–5, debate discussion and concluding interpretation
additional_scholarship.assessment: English capital-stock evidence differs across periods and interventions and also supports complementarity. It bounds extrapolation without contradicting the Massachusetts estimate.
additional_scholarship.next_step: Use different geography, outcomes and exposure definitions explicitly; do not pool the effect sizes.

lineage_checks: AGR-S04 inherits the Lansing historical narrative and reuses model/data lineage; it is not a second field confirmation of AGR-K05.
ANC-S06 overlaps Frontinus for relevant Roman aqueduct propositions; legal synthesis and ancient text are not two independent observations.
DIG-S09 extends the earlier Suri/Jack household data programme; earlier falsification tests are not independent replication.
LBR-K02 and LBR-K04 share the AT&T/census/cutover study and do not count as two independent replications.
Reconstructed engine stocks, capacity shares, colonial routes and Song output criticism were checked at the cited-author level; underlying historical datasets were not rebuilt.
NET-S11 explicitly traces a repeated historiographic claim rather than counting each repetition as independent corroboration.
limits: Twenty claims of 210 and 21 source records of 129 were passage-audited. No absence of defects can be generalized to the remaining records.
Access consistency concerns current availability and inspected support, not proof of every contributor’s historical reading behaviour.
Supplementary models, raw statistical data, original translated manuscripts and all upstream citations were not independently replicated.
Existing uncertain knowledge is not converted into a historical failure solely because evidence remains missing.
The current live programme and the separate external-R1 repair snapshot are outside this verdict.
